text:
eng-oncall-bot: PAGE triggered: smart-routing service alert — 5xx spike from edges in eu-central / ap-south. Severity: P1. Auto-escalating to oncall. links: http://pager/tree/1924000000
anya (sre): on it, looking at traces and routing decisions now. seeing increased fallback to eu-legacy-r1 variant from smart-router logs
marco (oncall): joining. what's the customer-facing impact?
anya (sre): error-rate ~12% for generate endpoints for ~6 minutes, tail latency also spiking. synthetic checks show traffic routed to eu-legacy-r1 which is returning 503s intermittently
ajay (platform): did a recent routing policy push go out? I pushed a small policy tweak to smartroute yesterday to prefer low-cost variants in asia/eu for certain model tags
sarah (network): DNS team — I'm seeing stale CNAMEs for eu-legacy-r1 in our edge resolver cache in a subset of POPs. TTLs were set to 300 but some resolvers still returning old A-records for ~1hr
anya (sre): hmm that could cause smartrouter's regional fallback to pick nodes that are decommissioned. logs show mismatch between model-variant metadata and available endpoints
marco (oncall): can we force smartroute to stop geo-fallback to eu-legacy-r1 as a mitigation?
ajay (platform): yes, we can toggle the routing policy to disable fallback targets. I'll prepare a quick rollback patch.
ops-bot: deploy started: policy-rollout/disable-eu-legacy-fallback by ajay — status: in-progress
anya (sre): meanwhile can someone run `dig +short eu-legacy-r1.edge.redwood.net` from affected POPs and post results? I want to confirm stale A records
sarah (network): from fra-pop-3: `dig +short eu-legacy-r1.edge.redwood.net @10.1.2.3` -> `203.0.113.12` (old), expected `198.51.100.77`
marco (oncall): that matches the hypothesis. some resolvers still have the old addresses cached despite the recent decommission.
ajay (platform): taking manual mitigation: patch applied to smartroute, disabling eu-legacy-r1 as a fallback target. ops-bot shows rollout complete
ops-bot: deploy finished: policy-rollout/disable-eu-legacy-fallback — status: success
anya (sre): traffic has started shifting away from eu-legacy-r1 in the router decisions. error-rate dropping from 12% -> 3% in the last 2 minutes
marco (oncall): great. can the DNS team force cache flush or lower negative TTLs for the affected records? Customers in AP-SOUTH still seeing some failures, maybe because their upstream resolvers have longer caching
sarah (network): we can't flush third-party resolvers but we can reduce authoritative TTL and re-publish. I've changed TTL to 60 and issued zone re-sign. Will monitor propagation. Also opened a support ticket with our CDN partner to purge edge cache for eu-legacy-r1 records
anya (sre): for immediate customer impact assessment: which customers saw errors? run query on request logs for 5xx grouped by org
marco (oncall): running query: `select org_id, count(*) as errors from requests where status>=500 and ts between now()-10m and now() group by org_id order by errors desc limit 50` -> org-412, org-7, org-99 top affected; collectively ~0.8% of total requests during window but higher for some orgs (org-412 ~12% of their traffic)
anya (sre): oncall-notify: @account-ops to surface to impacted customers: org-412 and org-7. Prepare message: brief incident note + mitigation steps + expected next update in 30m
marco (oncall): agreed. I'll draft and send now.
marco (oncall): message posted to customer-ops: "We're investigating increased 5xx rates affecting some generation requests in EU/AP regions. We've disabled a fallback target and traffic is rebalancing. We're monitoring and will update in 30 minutes. Impact: intermittent 5xx for a small subset of customers. If you're seeing persistent errors, please share request ids." :thumbsup:
anya (sre): monitoring: continue to watch smartroute decision logs for any re-introduction of stale variants. Also need to inspect why our decommissioning process left a reachable but unhealthy IP in authoritative DNS for longer than expected
ajay (platform): postmortem action: add a step in decommission playbook to `expire` variant from routing catalog before zone change, and add an automated check that ensures DNS records for decommissioned variants are removed from authoritative within 5m
sarah (network): action: investigate why some resolver caches ignored TTL updates — region-specific resolver behavior logged (fra-pop-3, bom-pop-1). I'll escalate with infra provider.
anya (sre): also adding an alert to detect sudden mismatch between routing_catalog.variants and authoritative DNS A records (TTL drift)
marco (oncall): current state: error-rate down to 1.1%, customer-impact limited but org-412 needs follow-up. handing off to oncall-next for monitoring and post-incident writeup
marco (oncall): @anya handing off — please own post-incident and summary
anya (sre): taking over. I'll collect traces, timeline, and open a postmortem doc. tentative severity: SEV2 (brief customer impact, quick mitigation)
ops-bot: incident closed for paging: smart-routing-P1 -> downgraded to SEV2 by anya
marco (oncall): thanks team. follow-ups: DNS TTL behavior, decommission playbook change, routing-catalog sync validation. we'll schedule a retro with platform + network next week.
anya (sre): notes for postmortem doc: timeline, mitigation commands used, logs excerpt, customer impact table, action items assigned to @ajay and @sarah. will post doc in #postmortems when ready.
marco (oncall): handoff complete. I'll stay in loop for 10 more minutes then step out.
anya (sre): thanks — will ping if anything regresses. :white_check_mark:
